body.statement: For every direction \(\lambda\), process columns \(w=H,H-1,\ldots,0\); when column \(w\) is reached, make rows \(b\le H-w\) eligible and allocate its remaining mass to eligible rows in decreasing \(c_b(\lambda)\), splitting only at exhausted row capacities. Whenever \(\Gamma_H(p,q)\ne\varnothing\), whose fixed-margin staircase feasibility is supported by Dahl2008, Theorem 4 after reversing the row order, the algorithm is feasible with no sign or monotonicity restriction on the induced real coefficients \(c_b(\lambda)\); it attains \(h_{\mathcal V}(\lambda)\), uses at most \(2H+1\) positive cells, and runs in \(O(H\log H)\) time with a heap.
body.justification: The attributed staircase theorem certifies the feasible domain, while the specialized exchange argument supplies a support oracle for the joint identified set and all pairwise regret calculations.
body.gap: HoffmanVeinott1993 supplies greedy staircase transportation results under superadditive rewards and cumulative capacities; this statement isolates the exchange property for every signed, potentially nonmonotone threshold-support direction needed here and is not positioned as an independent algorithmic novelty claim.
body.consumer: All robust threshold comparisons can be computed in time nearly linear in the cap rather than by a separate generic program for each pair.
